Vela doğrudan bu cihazdan Google uç noktalarıyla iletişim kurar: hesap yok, takip yok.

Vela’s own place data draws the businesses on the map, so panning around never asks Google, and it works offline. Which places lead is decided by what kind of place they are (hospitals, supermarkets, malls and campuses first), then brand and detail. Searching or tapping a place still goes to Google for hours, reviews and photos.

Google is asked for the places in view every time you pan. Nothing draws offline, and every pan sends your map position to Google. Google’s places are ranked by how many reviews they have, so the busiest name in a plaza takes the label even when it is not the anchor store.

Vela’s data draws the map, and once you stop panning one Google request adds anything it lacks. The extras show online only, and they arrive a beat after the map, so a few icons appear late and can take a label off a neighbor as they land.

Also shows the shops, restaurants and other businesses mapped in OpenStreetMap that Vela’s data lacks. OpenStreetMap edits appear here after the map tiles are rebuilt, usually within a week. On by default.

Tapping a place fetches its hours, reviews and photos from Google, and Vela remembers the match so the next tap is instant. Off = a tapped place shows only what Vela’s data has (name, type, address, phone, website) and nothing about the tap reaches Google. Search and directions still use Google.
Where Vela’s place data comes from

Vela’s place data is Overture Maps, an open dataset of businesses maintained by Meta, Microsoft and others, plus AllThePlaces, which collects chains from their own store locators, with OpenStreetMap correcting where each shop actually sits. Vela bakes the three into map tiles and serves them from its own GitHub repository, so nothing about where you look goes to Meta or Google.nnIt streams in as you browse and downloads with a region for offline use. Where Vela has no data for an area yet, the map falls back to Google.nnSearch, place details, hours, reviews and photos always come from Google, whichever option you pick.
